references.text: The immediate context: [ref:Luk 12:35-36|Luke 12:35-36] urges the disciples to be ready with their belts fastened and lamps burning, awaiting the return of the Lord – this is the background for the beatitude in verse 37.
[ref:Matt 24:46|Matthew 24:46] contains a parallel beatitude: "Blessed is that servant whom the master finds at work when he comes." The same theme of being found faithful at the Lord's coming.

[ref:Åp 3:20|Revelation 3:20] portrays Jesus as standing and knocking at the door, and whoever opens for him will share a meal with him – a similar motif where the Lord comes and shares fellowship with the faithful.

[ref:Luk 22:27|Luke 22:27] shows Jesus saying "I am among you as one who serves." The striking image in 12:37 of the Lord girding himself and serving his servants at the table points directly to Jesus' own act of service.

[ref:Joh 13:4-5|John 13:4-5] tells how Jesus rose from the meal, wrapped a towel around himself, and washed the disciples' feet. This is a concrete fulfillment of the image in Luke 12:37 where the Lord "girds himself and serves them".
[ref:Matt 25:21|Matthew 25:21] describes the reward given to the faithful servant: "Enter into the joy of your master!" The same theme that the Lord rewards those servants he finds faithful.
[ref:Mark 13:35-37|Mark 13:35-37] contains Jesus' exhortation to keep watch, for the master of the house may come at any time – a parallel motif about being awake (γρηγορέω) when the Lord comes.

[ref:Luk 12:43-44|Luke 12:43-44] continues with the parable of the faithful steward whom the master finds working, and who is then put in charge of all that the master owns – a continuation of the theme of reward for the watchful servants.
[ref:1 Tess 5:6|1 Thessalonians 5:6] exhorts: "Let us not sleep as others do, but let us stay awake and be sober." The same call to vigilance in light of the Lord's return.

[ref:1 Pet 1:13|1 Peter 1:13] uses the image "gird up the loins of your mind" (περιζώσασθε) – the same linguistic motif as in Luke 12:37 where the Lord girds himself, here applied to being mentally prepared for Christ's revelation.

[ref:Åp 19:9|Revelation 19:9] declares blessed those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb – an eschatological meal where the Lord shares fellowship with his own, parallel to the image in Luke 12:37.
